I play Compel the Spirit, moving the ally who 'has been burned since my
last turn' from my 'ash heap' to the active region.

Kherebutu then gets to lumber in for another attempt at bleeding.

As for the first point, the rules (6.4) state that a recruited ally is
placed in the inactive region. This is what stops him from acting. Compel
the spirit, on the other hand, does not even say that you are putting the
ally into play. It simply states 'Move the ally...to the active region
without paying the cost to put him or her into play.'. Incidentally, I
interperet Possession to work the same way, in that the resurrected
vampire is in the active region and is now free to act.

As for the second point, yes, things get a bit vague when referring to an
ally or retainer. Does it refer to the card or the 'character'? No one
would argue, I think, that all the 'Arcanum Investigators' represent
different allies and so when one gets a shotgun, they all don't get one.
By that logic though, if an Arcanum Investigator were to be burned, I
would surely be unable to play 'Compel the Spirit' to resurrect a
different Arcanum Investigator card. I would have to do the same
one. Right? Each card represents a unique individual so that no two
similar cards could be said to be 'the same ally'.

On the other hand, UNIQUE allies are different. The whole point of their
uniqueness is to clarify that in fact, every card represents the SAME
ally. If Kherebutu is burned, there can be no other Bane Mummy cards
hanging around the table. Surely though another player could then recruit
Kherebutu from his own hand and thus bring him back into play. The fact
that one Kherebutu card got shuffled back into my library does not affect
the way any other Kherebutu card can be played, except with regards to
the fact that another one could now be brought into play.

...and, because Kherebutu got burned, I can play Compel the Spirit and
look into my Ash heap for a Kherebutu card (any Kherebutu card). We ain't
playin' Vampire the Masquerade and nobody ever won a ame of Hearts
because they said that, "In Alice and Wonderland, the Queen of Hearts
couldn't die so I get my Queen back." Nope. Tis a game of rules rapes.
Tie them down and violate 'em messily.

;)

poke*poke

Messages.Author: James Puzzo
Messages.Body:
Malcolm McCallum (mcca...@tubby.pacificcoast.net) wrote:
: >
: As for the first point, the rules (6.4) state that a recruited ally is

: placed in the inactive region. This is what stops him from acting. Compel
: the spirit, on the other hand, does not even say that you are putting the
: ally into play. It simply states 'Move the ally...to the active region
: without paying the cost to put him or her into play.'. Incidentally, I
: interperet Possession to work the same way, in that the resurrected
: vampire is in the active region and is now free to act.

Hrrm. A sticky issue indeed. My gut reaction was to NOT believe that this
was the intent of the card, but after perusing my rule books and coming up
with:

Jyhad:

Cards that refer to vampires do not apply to allies. Cards that
refer to minions apply both to vampires and allies. Allies cannot
take an action on the turn recruited. When brought into play,
allies should be put in your inactive region to indicate that they
cannot act. At the end of your turn, allies in the inactive region
are moved to your active region.

VTES:

An ally cannot take an action on the turn he is recruited. When
the ally is brought into play, he is placed in your inactive
region to indicate that he cannot act. At the end of your turn,
allies in your inactive region are moved to your active region.

..which leads me to believe, as you do, that the card text stating that the
ally should be moved to the ACTIVE region would BREAK the rule stating that
the ally is placed in your inactive region when recruited. The question is
whether that line of reasoning should carry us to believe that it means
that "if an ally is placed directly into your active region, it can take
an action during that turn".

I am hard pressed to argue either way, since I've always read the rule
that "An ally cannot take an action on the turn he is recruited." as a
hard and fast rule, and that the extra text afterwards is simply a
method for one to remind oneself that it can't act, yet.

In other words, we need a ruling. :(

-spongy

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
An "ally who was burned since your last turn" is the ally *card* that was
burned since your last turn. It does not mean any other ally card, even
if the two cards share the same name, and even if they're unique allies.

Tom Wylie rec.games.trading-cards.* Network Representative for
aa...@cats.ucsc.edu Wizards of the Coast, Inc.

Messages.Author: eric liu
Messages.Body:
>..which leads me to believe, as you do, that the card text stating that the
>ally should be moved to the ACTIVE region would BREAK the rule stating that
>the ally is placed in your inactive region when recruited. The question is
>whether that line of reasoning should carry us to believe that it means
>that "if an ally is placed directly into your active region, it can take
>an action during that turn".
>
>I am hard pressed to argue either way, since I've always read the rule
>that "An ally cannot take an action on the turn he is recruited." as a
>hard and fast rule, and that the extra text afterwards is simply a
>method for one to remind oneself that it can't act, yet.
>
>In other words, we need a ruling. :(

It seems quite clear from the rules in both Jyhad and V:TES that for a
"Recruit Ally" action, the ally may take no actions on the turn it is put
into play.

HOWEVER, a "Compel the Spirit" action is NOT a "Recruit Ally" action, so
why should the former action be bound by the rules of the latter? They
may have related end results: both result in the introduction of an ally
to the game (though from different sources, the ash heap vs. one's hand),
but they ARE distinct from one another in much the same way that a bleed
+1 action with Social Charms is distinct from a bleed +1 action by the
Malkavian called Ozmo even though both actions have the same net effect.

It would therefore seem reasonable to say that if "Compel the Spirit" puts
the ally into the active region during a Methuselah's minion phase and that
ally is not tapped, then that ally should be able to take an action.

In any case, even IF there was a genuine conflict here and the card text
violated the rulebook text, wouldn't that still be perfectly legal? Is it
not the case that card text overrules rulebook text when a conflict arises
between the two?

ejl

Messages.Author: James Puzzo
Messages.Body:
eric liu (hect...@huey.csun.edu) wrote:
: >I am hard pressed to argue either way, since I've always read the rule

: >that "An ally cannot take an action on the turn he is recruited." as a
: >hard and fast rule, and that the extra text afterwards is simply a
: >method for one to remind oneself that it can't act, yet.
: >
: >In other words, we need a ruling. :(
:
: It seems quite clear from the rules in both Jyhad and V:TES that for a
: "Recruit Ally" action, the ally may take no actions on the turn it is put
: into play.

Yes.

: HOWEVER, a "Compel the Spirit" action is NOT a "Recruit Ally" action, so

: why should the former action be bound by the rules of the latter?

This is a point well taken. However, when looking for clarification on whether
or not this ally may then act, the only relevant information in the rules is
the information regarding ally recruitment. It is fine for card text to
change rules, but this card, provided it truly should be regarded as NOT
being a recruit ally action, provides a completely new TYPE of action, and
needs to be adequately explained, IMHO.

: They may have related end results: both result in the introduction

: of an ally to the game (though from different sources, the ash heap
: vs. one's hand), but they ARE distinct from one another in much the
: same way that a bleed +1 action with Social Charms is distinct from
: a bleed +1 action by the Malkavian called Ozmo even though both
: actions have the same net effect.

The difference is that the Social Charms action and the bleed by Ozmo are
BOTH "bleed" actions and are identifiable as such, and are goverened by the
rules _except_ in the parts that are possibly modified by card text. The
rules lay down very specific guidelines on what happens when one bleeds,
regardless of card text. The card text modifies this type of action.

I argue that "Compel the Spirit" is a different situation entirely.

If I am to disregard the rules on "recruiting" through the use of "Compel
the Spirit", I need to have the complete rules for the use of the card
spelled out in the card text, because there are no _underlying_ rules to
modify. If am to regard "Compel the Spirit" as a "modification" of the
rules for "recruiting", then I need a clarification on whether the card
text of "CtS" may be interpreted as overriding the very specific rules
text which states that "An ally may not an action on the turn he is
recruited", because the card text does not address this specifically.

In either case, I would be justified in asking for a clarification.

: It would therefore seem reasonable to say that if "Compel the Spirit" puts

: the ally into the active region during a Methuselah's minion phase and that
: ally is not tapped, then that ally should be able to take an action.

I don't think this is unreasonable... in fact, I feel that the card may
VERY reasonably be interpreted this way. I just do not feel that this is
the only interpretation, and that one who views the game in terms of "the
rules are law, and may only be broken by very specific card text", it is
also VERY reasonable to draw the conclusion that CtS brings the ally into
the active region, but that the ally MUST wait until the next turn because
the only relevant ruling in the rulebook states as much.

: In any case, even IF there was a genuine conflict here and the card text

: violated the rulebook text, wouldn't that still be perfectly legal? Is it
: not the case that card text overrules rulebook text when a conflict arises
: between the two?

It would CERTAINLY be perfectly legal... IF (I repeat, IF) the card text
can be read as _directly_ conflicting with the rulebook text. In the
rulebook there is a sentence which reads "An ally may not take an action on
the turn in which he is recruited" (roughly, I quoted it exactly in my
prior post). The card text says that an ally may be moved to the active
region. I do not see that the card text necessarily conflicts with the
sentence from the rules WITHOUT a ruling on the card text.

Once again:

If I am to read "Compel the Spirit" as simply modifying the "recruiting"
guidelines, I do NOT see that the card text "overrides" the very direct
statement stating that recruited allies may not take an action on the
turn in which they are recruited.

If I am to read "Compel the Spirit" as providing a completely NEW way of
bringing allies into the game (i.e. NOT by recruiting them), then I do not
believe that ANY of the recruiting rules may be seen as applying, and we
would STILL need clarification with regards to the card because the card
text does not adequately define the behavior of this new action.

And so I ask again... ruling please?

-spongy

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
The only reason that allies cannot act the turn they are recruited is that
they are recruited into your inactive region, rather than your ready region,
and don't come out until the end of the influence phase. By that time,
their chance to act that turn has passed.

If an effect such as Compel the Spirit just dumps an ally into play, then it
dumps it into the ready region, so the ally may act that turn.



In the case of the "Slimy Loophole" scenario, where a discarded Kherebutu
is the object of a "Compel the Spirit" action, does the discarded
Kherebutu count as an "ally who was burned since your last turn?"

Or more directly: Is a card that is discarded considered burned?

Is the "burned" status of the discarded Kherebutu equivalent to the
"burned" status of the Kherebutu that was burned to kill a Tremere?

And if so, how then does the card text (stating that if Kherebutu is burned he
is to be reshuffled into the Methuselah's library) relate to "burning"
Kherebutu via a simple discard? (I imagine a situation where you discard
Kherebutu, he is considered "burned," and you then replace him in your
library to be re-used: an eternal card).

If a discarded ally is not the same as a "burned" ally, then it would seem
that the "Slimy Loophole" combo could not be legal since the discarded
Kherebutu in the ash heap is not a valid candidate for a "Compel the
Spirit" action. Is this not the case?

ejl

Yes, but the reason is also given. An ally, when recruited, is placed

conflict, no relation.

No ruling needed.

> I argue that "Compel the Spirit" is a different situation entirely.
>

No you don't. Compel the Spirit says that it puts the ally into play,
and doesn't say that it puts the ally into your inactive region. Hence, since
it doesn't say that it is a recruit ally action, NONE of the recruit ally
rules apply. It simply puts the ally into your controlled region, end of story.

> I don't think this is unreasonable... in fact, I feel that the card may
> VERY reasonably be interpreted this way. I just do not feel that this is
> the only interpretation, and that one who views the game in terms of "the
> rules are law, and may only be broken by very specific card text", it is
> also VERY reasonable to draw the conclusion that CtS brings the ally into
> the active region, but that the ally MUST wait until the next turn because
> the only relevant ruling in the rulebook states as much.
>

No. The only relevant rule says that a newly recruited ally goes into
your inactive region, and hangs around for awhile until going into play during
your influence phase. This isn't a recruit ally action, if it was, it would
say "Recruit an ally from your ash heap, if it left play since your last turn.
You do not have to pay the cost of this ally" However, you will notice the
distinct LACK of any such text on that card.

>
> And so I ask again... ruling please?
>

Fine: "You may use an ally the turn it is brought into play via Compel
the Spirit."

> -spongy
